teams.heading: Jake White names four uncapped players for Fiji's Japan Test
teams.body: Jake White has named his first Fiji squad for Saturday's Test against Japan, according to Planet Rugby, and it includes four uncapped players. Nacani Boginisoko and Aporosa Vuniyayawa are in the starting XV, while Peni Naruma and Kavekini Boselawa could make their debuts off the bench. It is White's first Test in charge, and it opens preparation for November's Nations Championship matches against France, Ireland and Italy. Japan beat Fiji 20-15 in September's Pacific Nations Cup final, the first time the two have met since.

lead.why: It is a new men's squad and selection story about Fiji's own first Test under Jake White, and no earlier edition has run it.

teams.heading: Maro Itoje rejects French interest with new Saracens deal, safeguarding England future
teams.body: Maro Itoje has agreed a new Saracens deal, turning down mooted moves to Perpignan and Bordeaux and committing to a club he first represented in 2013. His existing contract was due to expire after next year's World Cup; the new terms are believed to run until 2029. The extension will let Itoje, who has 102 caps, continue his international career, and he was rested for England's summer Tests against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina after showing signs of fatigue. "He is staying," Brendan Venter said.

lead.why: It is the only England-player news item in the shortlist with a concrete event, and it has not been run before.

teams.heading: France hit by six major absences before Springboks Test in Paris
teams.body: Reports ahead of the Springboks Test in Paris put France's absences at six major injuries. AFP's account of the 42-man squad names Julien Marchand, Thibaud Flament, Emmanuel Meafou, Thomas Ramos and Matthieu Jalibert as injured so far this season. The squad was named this week, with flanker Gregory Alldritt back after a year away. Galthié has filled the gaps with uncapped players, including prop Karl Sorin.

teams.heading: London Irish, the Exiles club, target 2027 return after Steve Daniels takeover
teams.body: This is a club story, not an Ireland one: London Irish, out of action since going into administration in June 2023, hope to return as early as next season under new owner Steve Daniels. Balls, the chief executive, says they would welcome a Championship place, England's second tier, at the earliest opportunity. The club previously explored joining the United Rugby Championship, a competition featuring teams from Ireland, but met resistance within the game.

lead.why: The November squad is already reported, and this is the only fresh men's-adjacent item with a clear rugby angle, though it is a club story.

teams.heading: Scotland rise in world rankings despite no match since Fiji win
teams.body: The rise comes with Scotland on the sidelines, having last played when they beat Fiji 33-17 in Round three. It is a sign of how far a side can climb without taking the field. Their Nations Championship record reads two wins and one defeat from three, with 108 points scored, 97 conceded and a difference of +11. Their next fixture is Round four against New Zealand.

teams.heading: James Botham scores brace but Cardiff fall 36-21 to Sharks in URC
teams.body: Wales back-row James Botham was the standout figure as Cardiff slipped to a 36-21 United Rugby Championship defeat to the Sharks on Friday. The 28-year-old scored a brace and, by Planet Rugby's account, emptied the tank on both sides of the ball, while Cardiff led 21-17 midway through the second half before fading in the final quarter. Sharks won despite losing captain Andre Esterhuizen to a foot injury after 52 seconds, with Ethan Hooker and Matt Romao among their try-scorers.

teams.heading: Teddy Wilson earns maiden Wallabies call-up for spring Nations Championship Tests
teams.body: Waratahs scrum-half Teddy Wilson is one of two uncapped players in Les Kiss's 33-man squad for the Northern Hemisphere leg, with prop Tom Lambert the other, Planet Rugby reports. Wilson is the son of David Wilson, who won 79 Tests and was part of the 1999 World Cup-winning side. "I always want to make my family proud," he said. Ryan Lonergan has established himself as the standout No 9 in the squad.

lead.why: A new squad story about a maiden Wallabies call-up that has not yet run in this edition series, and it is the freshest men's Test item in the shortlist.

teams.heading: Japan lose 34-28 to Fiji in JRFU centenary Test in Tokyo
teams.body: Japan lost 34-28 to Fiji in the JRFU 100th Anniversary Match at Chichibunomiya Rugby Stadium, Tokyo, a little over a month after the Brave Blossoms beat the same opponents in the Pacific Nations Cup final. The sides were level at 21-all at half-time, and Fiji's Terio Tamani restored their lead in the 44th minute before Japan levelled at 28-all. Ben Volavola's penalties in the 60th and 69th minutes settled it, according to Fiji Sun's match report. The result avenges Fiji's September Pacific Nations Cup final defeat.

lead.why: A new result in Japan's centenary Test, reported after the preview that ran earlier today, and it reverses the September Pacific Nations Cup final.

teams.heading: Shannon Frizell, Samisoni Taukei'aho and Tyrel Lomax ruled out of Europe tour
teams.body: Three All Blacks are out of the European tour after the second Bledisloe Test in Sydney, according to SA Rugby Magazine. Shannon Frizell faces six weeks on the sidelines after rupturing the posterior cruciate ligament in his left knee, while hooker Samisoni Taukei'aho is expected to be out four to six weeks with a torn calf muscle. Prop Tyrel Lomax, battling a neck disc injury since Super Rugby, will stay in New Zealand for treatment. Richie Mo'unga, who missed both Bledisloe Tests, is not yet ruled out.

lead.why: A fresh injury blow to the current All Blacks squad ahead of the European tour, and the only new men's national-team item in the shortlist that is not a repeat.

teams.heading: Ethan Hooker scores as Sharks beat Cardiff 36-21 without captain Esterhuizen
teams.body: Ethan Hooker moved into the centres after Andre Esterhuizen went off inside the first minute, then scored the Sharks' opening try in their 36-21 bonus-point win at Cardiff. Planet Rugby called him "such a quality operator", and Siya Masuku came on for Jurenzo Julius at half-time. Rassie Erasmus is expected to name his squad for the Nations Championship tour in the coming days, and Esterhuizen's foot is a concern for the Springboks.

lead.why: It is the top-ranked new item in the shortlist, and it gives a fresh South Africa angle on the Esterhuizen injury without repeating it.
